hints.title: Non-Attacking Placement Obstacle
hints.text: Placing N queens on an NxN board without any two queens sharing a row, column, or diagonal requires avoiding invalid board states. How can tracking occupied diagonals prune conflicting placements in constant time?

hints.title: Diagonal Invariant Formulation
hints.text: Two cells (r1, c1) and (r2, c2) share a major diagonal if r1 - c1 == r2 - c2, and share an anti-diagonal if r1 + c1 == r2 + c2.

hints.title: Row-by-Row Placement Procedure
hints.text: Recurse row by row from 0 to n. For row r, iterate column c from 0 to n - 1. If c is in occupied columns, (r - c) in occupied diagonals, or (r + c) in occupied anti-diagonals, skip. Otherwise record state, place queen, recurse on r + 1, and backtrack by clearing sets.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def solveNQueens(self, n: int) -> List[List[str]]:
        res = []
        cols = set()
        diag1 = set()   # r - c
        diag2 = set()   # r + c
        board = [['.' for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]
        def backtrack(r: int):
            if r == n:
                res.append([''.join(row) for row in board])
                return
            for c in range(n):
                if c in cols or (r - c) in diag1 or (r + c) in diag2:
                    continue
                cols.add(c)
                diag1.add(r - c)
                diag2.add(r + c)
                board[r][c] = 'Q'
                backtrack(r + 1)
                board[r][c] = '.'
                cols.remove(c)
                diag1.remove(r - c)
                diag2.remove(r + c)
        backtrack(0)
        return res
```

variables: N: board dimension and queen count (1 <= N <= 9)
complexity.notes: First queen has N choices, second has at most N-2 choices, bounding complexity by O(N!).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all (N^2 choose N) board arrangements exceeds feasible computation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant-time diagonal state lookups require O(N) auxiliary set memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using row-by-row placement to inherently satisfy the row constraint.
